method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 45 covers L/M/M 1/2/N and sheet 46 covers N/N 1/2/O/O 1/2, so Avenue N is the only shared corridor; both plates print 'AVENUE N.' in this gutter and each prints the other's number beside it ('46' on sheet 45, '45' on sheet 46). The 22nd/23rd St hundred-block run changes exactly here: on sheet 45 the block against the avenue reads 1401/1403/1405/1407/1409/1411 and 1413/1415/1417/1419/1421/1423 with evens 1402-1412 and 1414/1416/1418/1420/1422/1424; on sheet 46 the block on the far side starts fresh at 1501/1503/1505/1507/1509/1511 with 1502/1504/1506/1508/1510/1512, then 1513-1529 / 1514-1528, and only after the next (half) avenue does it reach 1601/1603/1605/1607 and 1602/1604/1606/1608. So 14xx->15xx is this avenue and 15xx->16xx is Ave N 1/2, one block east. The avenue frontage runs interlock across the same gutter: sheet 45's east block face carries evens 2202,2204,2206...2218 and sheet 46's west block face the odds 2201,2203,2205...2217 - the two sides of the 22nd-23rd segment of Avenue N.
note: Detection candidates (45: 2759/1740/722; 46: 778/1778/2779) are mid-block lines. '70'' is printed mid-avenue on sheet 45 beside this gutter; sheet 46's Scale of Feet bar measures 3.01 native px/ft (0/50/100/150 ft ticks at native x 590.0/738.5/889.5/1041.5), so 70' = 211 px, half = 105.5. Sheet 45 west face 3031 + 105.5; sheet 46 east face 282 - 105.5.
